result:
A title edit updates a separate search row in the same request that saves the issue. A later search reads that row, and a query that looks fine can still be rejected for plan, rate, or permission reasons before any match runs.

## How the searchable copy stays in step

Saving a title goes through `updateIssueAction` in `src/actions/issues/update-issue.ts`. `withAction` parses the body with `updateIssueSchema` and resolves the `Actor`. The action then calls `can(actor, "issue:update", …)` and `updateIssue` in `src/server/services/issue-service.ts`.

`updateIssue` checks the tenant with `assertOrgScope`, loads the row with `issueRepo.findIssueById`, checks `assertCan(actor, "issue:update", …)` against that row, and refuses an archived issue via `assertNotArchived`. Only then does `issueRepo.updateIssue` write the new `title` (and any other fields present on the input) onto the `issues` table. The service does not touch the search table itself. It publishes `issue.updated` through `emit` in `src/lib/event-bus.ts`, with an `EventEnvelope` plus `issueId`, `projectId`, and `changedFields`. The payload carries no title.

`emit` waits for every subscriber (`Promise.allSettled`), so the search update finishes before `updateIssue` returns. Those subscribers are attached once per server process: `register` in `src/instrumentation.ts` calls `registerEventHandlers` in `src/server/services/event-registry.ts`, which calls `registerSearchListeners` in `src/server/services/search-service.ts`.

The `issue.updated` handler ignores the event body as a source of text. It calls `issueRepo.findIssueById` again and, if that row exists, `indexIssue`. `indexIssue` builds one string, `title` and `description` joined by a newline, and passes it to `searchRepo.upsertSearchDocument`. The same listener set also indexes `issue.created`, `comment.created`, and `project.created`, and deletes the document on `issue.archived`, `comment.deleted`, and `project.archived`. A `search.reindex_requested` handler re-reads and reindexes issues only. Nothing in the app emits that event. The daily `search-reindex` job in `src/server/jobs/search-reindex-job.ts` can rebuild one org by walking projects, issues, and comments and calling `indexProject`, `indexIssue`, and `indexComment`, but the scheduler enqueues it with an empty payload, and `runHandler` in `src/server/jobs/queue.ts` returns immediately unless `payload.orgId` is a string. The path that makes a new title searchable is the `issue.updated` listener, not that job.

`upsertSearchDocument` in `src/server/repositories/search-repository.ts` is idempotent on `(orgId, subjectKind, subjectId)`. It selects an existing `search_index` row with `orgPredicate` and, if one exists, updates `content`, `projectId`, and `indexedAt`. Otherwise it inserts a new row with `newId()`.

## What that copy stores

The table is `searchIndex` (`search_index`) in `src/server/db/schema/webhooks.ts`, typed as `SearchIndexRow`. Each row has:

- `id`, a ULID primary key
- `orgId` (`org_id`)
- `subjectKind`: `"issue"`, `"comment"`, or `"project"`
- `subjectId`
- `projectId`, nullable; for an issue this is the issue's project, for a comment it is null, for a project it is the project's own id
- `content`, the only searchable text
- `indexedAt`, an ISO timestamp

For an issue, `content` is the title, a newline, and the description (empty string when there is none). There is no separate title column, and status, assignee, labels, and priority are not copied. A secondary index covers `(orgId, subjectKind)`. At read time the hit title is the first line of `content`.

## What a query goes through

Three callers share `search` in `src/server/services/search-service.ts`.

The search page at `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/search/page.tsx` loads the tenant, evaluates `advanced_search` with `isEnabled` and `buildFlagContext`, and parses `q` with `searchQuerySchema` (`src/schemas/search.ts`: `q` is 1–200 characters, `kinds` defaults to `["issue"]`, optional `projectId`, plus `limit` 1–100 and an optional cursor from `pageRequestSchema`). On the enterprise plan it asks for issue, comment, and project; otherwise it asks for issues only. It then calls `search` directly.

`searchAction` in `src/actions/search/search.ts` goes through `withAction` (schema, then `requireActorFor`), requires `can(actor, "org:read", …)`, loads the org, and if `advanced_search` is off drops every kind other than `"issue"` before calling `search`. `SearchDialog` in `src/components/domain/search/search-dialog.tsx` is the client of that action. It debounces the input and runs `parseSearchQuery` in `src/components/domain/search/query-syntax.ts`. With the flag on, `kind:` / `in:` and `project:` are pulled out into `kinds` and `projectId`, and the free-text remainder is what gets sent as `q`. With the flag off, the whole string is sent as free text and `kinds` stays `["issue"]`.

`GET` in `src/app/api/search/route.ts` requires `orgSlug` and `q`, loads the actor with `getActor`, requires `org:read`, requires the `command_palette` flag, forces kinds the same way as the page, caps `limit` at 10, and calls `search`.

Inside `search` the order is fixed:

1. `assertOrgScope(actor, input.orgId)` in `src/lib/tenant.ts`.
2. `assertCan(actor, "issue:read", orgResource(input.orgId))`. Viewers and above have `issue:read`.
3. `consumeRateLimit(input.orgId, "search:query")` in `src/lib/rate-limit.ts`. The bucket's base shape is 120 tokens, refilled at 60 per minute, scaled by the org plan's `apiRequestsPerHour`.
4. `orgRepo.findOrgById`, then `isEnabled("advanced_search", …)`. That flag, defined in `src/config/feature-flags.ts`, is on for the enterprise plan, or when `org.settings.enabledFlagOverrides` lists it.
5. If `q` contains `:` and the flag is off, `search` throws `Field-scoped search is not included in this plan`.
6. `searchRepo.searchDocuments` filters with `orgPredicate`, `like(content, %q%)`, an optional `subjectKind` `inArray`, and an optional `projectId`. An empty `kinds` array adds no kind filter. It counts, then returns a keyset page ordered by `indexedAt` descending, then `id` descending.
7. Each row becomes a `SearchHit`: `title` is the first line of `content`, `snippet` is `snippetAround` (60 characters on either side of a case-insensitive match), and `href` is `/issues/{id}`, `/comments/{id}`, or `/projects/{id}`.

The server never interprets `status:` or similar. Field syntax is only the dialog splitting `kind`/`in`/`project` off before the request. A colon that still arrives in `q` is either rejected or matched as literal text.

## When a normal-looking query is refused

`searchQuerySchema` already accepts any string from 1 to 200 characters, so these are refusals of input that has passed shape checks.

A `q` that contains a colon is rejected whenever `advanced_search` is off, including a title someone is trying to match literally (`API: timeout`) and a field-shaped string (`status:done`). The growth-plan test in `tests/services/search-service.test.ts` expects exactly that throw. The dialog makes this easy to hit: with the flag off, `parseSearchQuery` forwards the raw string, colon included. The search page's helper text says comments and projects open on the growth plan; the flag that both widens `kinds` and allows a colon is enterprise (or an org override).

The same function rejects a well-formed query when the `search:query` bucket is empty, with `Search rate limit reached; try again after ${resetAt}`.

Before that function runs, the action and the route return forbidden when `can` denies `org:read`. The route also returns forbidden when `command_palette` is off, and `validation_failed` when `orgSlug` or `q` is missing or the schema rejects the payload (for example `q` longer than 200 characters, which the page renders as "That query is not valid"). Inside `search`, a mismatched `orgId` throws `TenantScopeError` from `assertOrgScope`, and a role below viewer fails `assertCan` for `issue:read`. `withAction` and `errorResponse` turn those throws into the action or JSON error envelope. Asking for comments or projects on a plan without `advanced_search` is narrowed to issues (or, on the action, to an empty `kinds` list, which then matches every kind) rather than rejected.
